title: QUIC Interop Harness Adapter and Endpoint Host Contract
purpose: Define the interop-runner-facing companion harness contract that hosts Incursa.Quic without moving protocol/runtime ownership out of the main library.
scope: This slice covers the harness project shape, runner environment parsing, mounted path mapping, endpoint-host shell plumbing, handshake testcase dispatch, reserved-version versionnegotiation dispatch, the smaller post-handshake-stream child-process contract, the narrow retry child-process contract, the sequential multiconnect child-process contract, unsupported testcase exit behavior, the ordered transfer-owned child-process completion contract, qlog snapshot hooks, the repo-local execution-report helper, the repo-local preflight planner and localhost smoke lane, split client/server local execution modes, Docker packaging, manual hosted interop-runner corroboration, advisory hosted supported-subset matrix planning, the manual major peer matrix for currently executable non-HTTP/3 scenarios and the generated inventory/evidence reports, the documented non-HTTP/3 testcase inventory/profile, the bounded QUIC interop-runner `http3` endpoint adapter, the advisory external HTTP/3 peer harness, the advisory h3spec HTTP/3 server conformance pipeline, the ProtocolLab package producer boundary, and CI participation.
context: Incursa.Quic remains the owner of reusable transport/runtime behavior. The interop harness owns process-facing adapter concerns, including runner environment parsing, mounted path mapping, role dispatch, process exit behavior, endpoint-host composition, local preflight planning, optional hosted corroboration, and inventory publication. Supported server-role dispatch paths derive responses from observed HTTP/0.9 request targets rather than relying on server-side `REQUESTS` values except for the bounded HTTP/3 runner cell, where the HTTP/3 layer decodes request HEADERS and maps the request path to `/www`. The `versionnegotiation` cell uses a reserved unsupported client version so the server can elicit Version Negotiation on the documented root request target without a transfer-path dependency. Long-running supported paths avoid initiating application close before the peer closes or a bounded timeout expires. Library-owned protocol behavior remains traced through the CRT, RFC, HTTP/3, and QPACK requirement families; this INT specification owns only the harness adapter, inventory, artifact, package-producer, and runner-facing contracts. The non-HTTP/3 inventory/profile requirement records the required classification model and artifact-retention contract without turning current execution status into normative requirement text. The `http3` runner cell is now a bounded adapter slice; broader HTTP/3, QPACK dynamic table, server push, trailers, CONNECT, HTTP Datagrams, MASQUE, and ASP.NET hosting behavior remain outside this INT specification. The ProtocolLab package producer uses public ProtocolLab tooling and contract/model surfaces as an external package contract seam while keeping concrete quic-dotnet adapter and server implementation source local to this repository.
open_questions: When a real TLS provider is selected, what is the practical path for optional SSLKEYLOGFILE support without leaking provider-specific details into the harness?

supplemental_sections.heading: Endpoint Host Contract
supplemental_sections.content: The endpoint-host shell bridges library-owned runtime connections through the UDP socket boundary while keeping runner-facing concerns in the harness. Supported server-role paths tolerate an empty server-side `REQUESTS` list by deriving response targets from observed HTTP/0.9 request lines, `versionnegotiation` uses the documented root request target together with a reserved unsupported client version, and long-running supported paths avoid server-initiated application close before peer close or a bounded timeout. Unsupported testcases return exit code `127`.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary Split
supplemental_sections.content: Library-owned concerns include connection runtime, sender and recovery ownership, TLS-facing transport state, packet protection lifecycle, handshake confirmation, retransmission planning, timer ownership, path-state ownership, packet open/protect helpers, and transport-visible diagnostics hooks. Endpoint-host concerns include the connected UDP socket lifecycle, receive loop, effect-to-socket send plumbing, and ingress/transition/effect observers. Harness-owned concerns include environment parsing, mounted path mapping, role dispatch, process exit codes, Docker packaging, startup scripts, and the thin endpoint-host shell wrapper.

supplemental_sections.heading: Local Execution Loop
supplemental_sections.content: The repo-local helper keeps the external interop runner unmodified, builds the harness image locally, and uses the runner's image-replacement path to capture JSON, Markdown, and log artifacts under `artifacts/interop-runner/...` without requiring a registry change in the runner repository. It supports same-slot both-role runs as well as split client/server runs that replace only the local side and leave the opposite side on an established implementation such as quic-go or msquic. The `versionnegotiation` cell uses the same helper path but does not rely on file-transfer path derivation.

supplemental_sections.heading: Hosted Corroboration
supplemental_sections.content: The manual hosted workflow defaults to the narrow server-role `handshake` helper cell against a quic-go client slot and uploads the full artifact bundle regardless of result. It also offers an explicit `supported-subset` profile that fans out over already-supported helper cells for retry, transfer, and multiconnect evidence collection, an explicit `major-peer-matrix` profile that exercises the currently executable non-HTTP/3 role/peer cells against quic-go and msquic, and an explicit `zerortt-server-proof` profile that targets only the server-role zerortt attempt on hosted Linux so the runner can produce evidence beyond the Windows long-filename setup blocker. These profiles are intentionally advisory and are not part of push, pull-request, or package gating.

supplemental_sections.heading: Documented Non-HTTP/3 Inventory
supplemental_sections.content: The upstream QUIC testcase inventory is tracked as a distinct profile goal. The inventory/profile classifies each documented non-HTTP/3 testcase as supported and executed, intentionally unsupported, prerequisite-blocked, or not mappable through the current helper/workflow. Those classification values are evidence outputs, not broad support promises, and HTTP/3 stays out of scope.

supplemental_sections.heading: HTTP/3 Runner Cell
supplemental_sections.content: The `http3` interop-runner cell is owned as a bounded adapter over the existing managed QUIC transport and the standalone HTTP/3/QPACK modules. The endpoint image uses ALPN `h3`, runner-mounted `/certs`, `/www`, and `/downloads`, server UDP port 443, client `REQUESTS` downloads, and the runner's 0/1/127 exit contract. This does not promote broader HTTP/3 hosting, server push, trailers, CONNECT, HTTP Datagrams, MASQUE, or upstream-registry support claims.

supplemental_sections.heading: External HTTP/3 Peer Harness
supplemental_sections.content: The external HTTP/3 harness is a repo-local Docker Compose matrix for characterizing Incursa.Quic against peer HTTP/3 clients and servers outside the upstream QUIC interop runner. It produces JSONL results and Markdown reports with pass, fail, and skip states. Skipped rows are first-class evidence that a peer command or scenario endpoint has not been wired, not implicit support.

supplemental_sections.heading: h3spec Server Conformance Harness
supplemental_sections.content: The h3spec harness is a repo-local advisory pipeline for running h3spec against the Incursa HTTP/3 sample server, preserving stdout and stderr, parsing failing cases, mapping HTTP/3 and QPACK failures to RFC 9114 and RFC 9204 sections plus current gap owners, and producing a Markdown TODO report. It is a conformance triage surface and not a complete HTTP/3 or QPACK support claim.

supplemental_sections.heading: Standalone Local Preflight
supplemental_sections.content: The localhost preflight lane is now captured normatively in REQ-QUIC-INT-0014. It gives the repository a repo-local place to separate harness planning and smoke execution before the external runner or peer-implementation helper is involved.

requirements.title: Keep the interop endpoint in a companion project
requirements.statement: The interop endpoint MUST be implemented as a companion project that references `Incursa.Quic` rather than by turning the main library project into an application.
notes: The harness exists to host the library in the process shape expected by the interop runner.
Reusable transport behavior remains in the library.

requirements.title: Own runner-facing process plumbing in the harness
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST own parsing of `ROLE`, `TESTCASE`, `REQUESTS`, `QLOGDIR`, and `SSLKEYLOGFILE`, mapping of `/www`, `/downloads`, and `/certs`, role dispatch, and runner-facing process exit-code behavior. Supported server-role dispatch paths must still start when the runner provides an empty `REQUESTS` list.
notes: These concerns exist because of the interop runner contract and would not belong in the library.
Client-side dispatch still uses the first `REQUESTS` URL when one is present, but supported server-side dispatch paths must remain able to start without a request URL from the runner.

requirements.title: Return unsupported testcases honestly
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST return exit code `127` for any unsupported or not-yet-implemented interop testcase.

requirements.title: Keep qlog and keylog hooks honest
requirements.statement: When `QLOGDIR` is provided, the harness MUST emit contained qlog JSON snapshots for supported client and listener bootstrap paths without hardwiring the library to qlog JSON, and when `SSLKEYLOGFILE` is not yet practical it must remain a clear TODO rather than fake behavior.

requirements.title: Reject invalid runner configuration with failure status
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST reject invalid `ROLE`, missing `TESTCASE`, or other runner-configuration failures that prevent dispatch with exit code `1` instead of reporting unsupported success.

requirements.title: Bridge runtime-owned handshake packets through a real UDP socket shell
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST provide a thin endpoint-host shell that composes the library-owned connection runtime endpoint through a connected UDP socket, forwards inbound datagrams into the library ingress path, surfaces outbound datagram effects back to the socket layer, and keeps route misses and unsupported cases honest instead of fabricating transport success.
notes: The shell remains adapter-only: it owns socket/process lifecycle and observers, not protocol behavior.

The harness handshake testcase now routes through this seam; the narrow transfer slice now has its own managed active-phase path and the narrow retry slice now has its own managed one-Retry path plus the runner-generated single-request delivery gate.

requirements.title: Define the ordered transfer slice as narrow and proof-gated
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST define a child-process-only `transfer` slice on the existing Active-phase managed path in which one managed connection is established for the ordered space-separated `REQUESTS` URL list, exactly one application stream is opened per request in request order, the fixed `/www` and `/downloads` mount-path contract remains in force for every request, the existing `Http3` ALPN remains in force, and exit code `0` is considered honest only after byte delivery and EOF have completed for every ordered request on both sides. This slice must not widen retry, parallel or arbitrary multi-stream generalization, broader 1-RTT claims, trust-store policy, hostname validation, certificate-path validation, revocation, 0-RTT, or key update.
notes: This requirement owns only the managed child-process transfer boundary on the existing active path. It does not widen the public promise, `IsSupported`, or broader interop compatibility claims.

The current runtime already owns the ordered stream open, write, read, flow-control, and EOF mechanics on the supported active-loopback path; this requirement closes the harness-owned ordered file-pump completion contract and proof.

requirements.title: Sequence the first application stream open and accept after handshake
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST define a child-process-only `post-handshake-stream` testcase on the managed child-process harness path in which, after the existing handshake completes, the client opens the first application stream and the server accepts that first application stream. This requirement must remain limited to the managed child-process path and must not claim byte delivery, EOF completion, transfer enablement, retry enablement, multi-stream behavior, broader 1-RTT data-path readiness, trust-store policy widening, hostname validation, certificate-path validation, revocation, 0-RTT, or key update.
notes: The supported boundary remains unchanged; this slice proves only the first post-handshake application-stream open/accept sequence and does not claim file delivery, EOF, or transfer enablement.

The harness owns only the child-process sequencing proof. The runtime already owns the open and accept primitives, and the client opener path depends on the existing client-role 1-RTT readiness gate while the server accepter path depends on the existing active-phase accept gate.

requirements.title: Dispatch a single valid Retry through the child-process harness path
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST define a child-process-only `retry` testcase in which the server emits exactly one valid Retry, the client observes that Retry and reissues the next Initial through the already-landed managed replay handoff, the server accepts the replayed Initial on the real managed path, the client sends the runner-provided single HTTP/0.9 request after the post-Retry handshake completes, the server serves that mounted `/www` file on the same connection, the client writes it under `/downloads`, and exit code `0` is considered honest only after byte delivery and EOF complete for that retry request. This requirement must remain limited to the child-process retry path and must not claim public API widening, `IsSupported` widening, transfer generalization outside the retry testcase, multi-Retry behavior, broad token-lifecycle behavior, trust-store policy, hostname validation, certificate-path validation, revocation, broader client-auth, `0-RTT`, or key update.
notes: This slice proves the managed one-Retry child-process contract and the runner's single post-Retry file-delivery expectation only. It does not widen the public surface, `IsSupported`, broader transfer, or broader TLS policy.
The client replay side is already owned by the library bootstrap seam in REQ-QUIC-CRT-0122; this requirement owns the child-process dispatch and proof.

requirements.title: Capture local interop-runner execution reports without changing the runner registry
requirements.statement: The repository MUST provide a local helper that builds the `Incursa.Quic.InteropHarness` image and invokes the external `quic-interop-runner` locally against the already-supported interop testcase subset by replacing a local-side implementation image in either a same-slot both-role run or a split client/server run, and it must capture the runner's JSON, Markdown, and log artifacts without requiring any change to the runner repository's implementation registry.
notes: The helper is intentionally local-only and may use the runner's image-replacement mechanism rather than adding an Incursa.Quic entry to the runner repository.
Split-role runs should keep the opposite side on established implementations such as quic-go or msquic, while same-slot both-role runs remain supported for the local harness image.
The helper records execution-report artifacts; it does not introduce new testcase support or any new protocol behavior.

Any advisory-only downgrade for the runner's post-check `FileNotFoundError` must remain testcase-specific and evidence-backed by preserved local logs; unsupported, unproven, or ambiguous runs still fail honestly.

The helper's `keyupdate` and `resumption` FileNotFound downgrades require testcase-specific managed evidence markers, so the major peer matrix can preserve externally failed post-check bundles without hiding missing key-update initiation, missing resumed-connection proof, or incomplete endpoint exits.

requirements.title: Separate local preflight planning from localhost smoke execution
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST expose repo-local preflight decisions for request parsing, qlog selection, endpoint resolution, transfer-path mapping, and transfer-sized client receive-window selection as independently testable harness behavior, and must support a localhost smoke lane in which the managed client and managed server can be exercised directly with matching certificate names while preserving the existing hostname and certificate-validation rules. This slice must not weaken hostname or certificate validation for IP-literal hosts or require changes to the external `quic-interop-runner` repository.
notes: The preflight planner keeps request parsing, qlog selection, endpoint resolution, and transfer-path mapping available as direct local proofs.
The localhost smoke lane exists to separate harness and setup failures from library behavior without loosening certificate or hostname validation.

requirements.title: Dispatch multiconnect as sequential managed connections
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST define a child-process-only `multiconnect` testcase in which the ordered space-separated client `REQUESTS` URLs are interpreted as a sequential dispatch plan, one managed connection is opened per URL on the existing endpoint-host active-phase path, the client applies a bounded loss-tolerant per-connection handshake and idle budget for the external runner's `handshakeloss` scenario without changing the public default, the client sends exactly one HTTP/0.9 GET and downloads exactly one mounted response per connection, the server accepts one connection per URL and serves one mounted response per connection for ordered server-role `REQUESTS`, the server treats an empty server-role `REQUESTS` list as an open sequential accept plan that derives each mounted response path from the observed HTTP/0.9 request target, stalled responses fail the child process with exit code `1` rather than hanging behind the external runner timeout, and the slice does not claim parallel connection handling, generalized multipath routing, migration or rebinding support, retry enablement, `0-RTT`, key update, or any public API widening.
notes: The testcase stays on the same real endpoint-host transfer path as the existing transfer slice, but uses one HTTP/0.9 request and one response per connection instead of reusing the transfer slice's single-connection request loop.
The ordered `REQUESTS` list must fail honestly when it contains malformed input or conflicting host and port values.

A response that stops making progress after the request line is sent must leave the testcase in a failed state and clean up partial output instead of waiting indefinitely for the external runner to time out.

The multiconnect client timing override is limited to the child-process interop lane and must remain bounded so hosted handshakeloss evidence can distinguish packet-loss recovery from an unbounded hang.

Server-role open-plan support exists because the external runner supplies an empty `REQUESTS` list to the server side while the peer client still opens sequential connections and sends concrete HTTP/0.9 targets.

requirements.title: Provide a manual hosted interop-runner handshake corroboration lane
requirements.statement: The repository MUST provide a manually dispatched hosted-CI workflow that checks out both this repository and an external `quic-interop-runner` checkout, invokes the repo-local interop helper in server-role `handshake` mode against an established `quic-go` client slot, uploads the complete interop-runner artifact tree regardless of helper outcome, and keeps the lane advisory and outside ordinary push, pull-request, build, test, package, and support-readiness gates.
notes: The workflow exists to collect hosted artifacts for one narrow runner cell; it does not alter the runner repository, add a registry entry, or enable a broader matrix.
The helper's advisory classification remains evidence-backed by preserved logs, and the uploaded runner report can still show an upstream runner post-check failure.
A passed manual workflow run is not a claim that Incursa.Quic is QUIC-complete, interop-ready, or public-surface stable.

requirements.title: Provide a manual hosted interop-runner supported-subset coverage profile
requirements.statement: The repository MUST provide an explicit manually dispatched hosted-CI coverage profile that runs the repo-local interop helper over the already-supported external-runner helper subset, including the narrow server-role `handshake` cell, a bounded `retry` same-slot cell, split-role `transfer` cells, and the client-role `multiconnect` cell that maps to the runner `handshakeloss` testcase, while uploading a distinct artifact bundle for every attempted cell; this profile remains advisory, opt-in, outside ordinary push, pull-request, build, test, package, and support-readiness gates, and does not claim new protocol support, public API widening, runner registry participation, `post-handshake-stream` external-runner coverage, 0-RTT, key update, migration, or broad interop readiness.
notes: The default manual workflow profile stays the single hosted-handshake cell from REQ-QUIC-INT-0016.
The wider profile is a coverage and artifact-collection profile for helper-supported cells only; it is not a new testcase-support requirement.
The `post-handshake-stream` child-process testcase remains local harness coverage and is not exposed through the external-runner helper until a separate requirement authorizes that mapping.

requirements.title: Publish a non-HTTP/3 interop testcase inventory profile
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST publish and maintain a non-HTTP/3 testcase inventory/profile for the documented upstream QUIC interop suite, enumerate each documented QUIC testcase other than `http3`, classify each testcase as supported and executed, intentionally represented as unsupported, blocked by a named prerequisite, or not mappable through the current helper/workflow, preserve per-cell artifact retention for supported or intentionally represented cells, keep `http3` out of scope, and avoid any support-readiness promise or green implication for a listed cell.
notes: The documented upstream non-HTTP/3 suite currently includes versionnegotiation, handshake, transfer, longrtt, chacha20, multiplexing, keyupdate, retry, resumption, zerortt, amplificationlimit, blackhole, multiconnect, transferloss, ipv6, v2, rebind-port, rebind-addr, and connectionmigration. HTTP/3, corruption, and ECN cells remain outside this helper-supported inventory until a separate proof slice promotes them explicitly.
`http3` remains out of scope for this slice.

A testcase may be classified as intentionally unsupported or prerequisite-blocked while its underlying protocol slice is still red; that classification must be explicit rather than implied by a generic unsupported fallthrough.

requirements.title: Provide a manual major peer interop matrix profile
requirements.statement: The repository MUST provide an explicit manually dispatched hosted-CI major peer matrix profile that exercises Incursa.Quic as the local client and as the local server against the `quic-go` and `msquic` peer implementation slots for the currently executable non-HTTP/3 external-runner cells `handshake`, `retry`, `transfer`, `keyupdate`, and `resumption`, uploads a distinct artifact bundle for every attempted role, peer, and testcase cell, keeps `http3` and prerequisite-blocked inventory cells out of this profile, and remains advisory, opt-in, outside ordinary push, pull-request, build, test, package, and support-readiness gates.
notes: This profile is an evidence-collection surface, not a broad interop-readiness gate. The generated `interop-major-peer-matrix-inventory` report keeps the current cell set explicit, and the completed run `25904716076` now has the dedicated `interop-major-peer-matrix-evidence-25904716076` report that preserves its mixed peer-specific pass and failure classes.

`versionnegotiation` now has explicit reserved-version runner dispatch, but it remains excluded from the role-backed major peer matrix by profile scope, and the generated inventory/evidence reports stay limited to the current handshake, retry, transfer, keyupdate, and resumption cell set.

`rebind-port` and `rebind-addr` remain governed by their prerequisite-blocked inventory classifications under `REQ-QUIC-INT-0018`, while `v2`, `chacha20`, and `connectionmigration` are now supported/executed under that same inventory requirement and `zerortt` is now governed by `REQ-QUIC-INT-0021` as supported/executed.

requirements.title: Run versionnegotiation with a reserved client version
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST accept `versionnegotiation` on both client and server roles, treat the documented root `REQUESTS` URL as valid dispatch input, and drive the client through a reserved unsupported QUIC version so the server emits Version Negotiation and the client aborts the connection attempt, preserving the existing qlog capture, SSLKEYLOGFILE gating, and unsupported-testcase behavior without widening HTTP/3, 0-RTT, key update, resumption, or migration semantics.
notes: This slice makes the supported/executed inventory claim source-backed.
It does not expand the major-peer-matrix profile or change HTTP/3, 0-RTT, key update, resumption, or migration semantics.

requirements.title: Classify zerortt as supported/executed after hosted Linux proof succeeds
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST classify `zerortt` as supported/executed only when the advisory hosted Linux `zerortt-server-proof` profile completes end to end with packet-analysis evidence that 0-RTT request-stream data was sent and acted on, and not classify `zerortt` as supported/executed based on server-role dispatch, managed resumption tickets, internal early-data admission, local first-flight X25519 proof, managed response/download success, or any partial hosted proof alone.
notes: This is a classification gate, not a protocol-support promise. The gate is now closed by the preserved hosted Linux proof bundle, and partial hosted proof, internal runtime proof, or server-only dispatch remains insufficient on its own.

requirements.title: Provide a hosted connectionmigration proof lane
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST provide manual advisory hosted Linux `connectionmigration-server-proof` and `connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` profiles. The `connectionmigration-server-proof` profile exercises the server role against `neqo` by replacing a distinct local server slot, preserving `neqo-peer` as the reported peer alias, normalizing the actual runner peer slot to `neqo`, and using the `ghcr.io/mozilla/neqo-qns:latest` peer image for `connectionmigration`; the blocked companion profile keeps `ngtcp2`, `lsquic`, `quiche`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, and `aioquic` visible for comparison. Both profiles upload distinct artifact bundles for each cell and stay outside ordinary push, pull-request, build, test, package, and support-readiness gates. The proof profile preserves live corroboration for the already classified connectionmigration inventory cell and is not intended to be read as broad support for `rebind-port`, `rebind-addr`, or HTTP/3.
notes: This slice creates a dedicated hosted corroboration path for the connectionmigration lane and keeps the blocked comparison peers visible without widening the green proof lane.
It does not broaden the major-peer-matrix profile or change the underlying supported-executed helper inventory claim.

requirements.title: Formalize the quic-go client download-liveness slice
requirements.statement: The repository MUST keep the remaining Incursa-side major-peer candidate bounded to the `quic-go` client `transfer` and `keyupdate` drain path, complete the download when the known mounted source-length body has been transferred instead of waiting for peer EOF, preserve the bounded client download-liveness contract, keep the `msquic` `TLS alert 50` / termination cells outside that local candidate set, and avoid widening into a generic keepalive policy, server-role behavior, or a broad public API rewrite.
notes: This slice formalizes the bounded client download completion boundary for the current quic-go candidate.
It does not widen into server-role behavior, a generic keepalive policy, or broader msquic support.

requirements.title: Classify the msquic major-peer failures as peer-side blocked evidence
requirements.statement: The repository MUST keep the `msquic` major-peer evidence cluster classified as peer-side blocked evidence when the preserved major-peer run records `peer-tls-alert-50` or `peer-connection-terminated` outcomes across the `handshake`, `retry`, `transfer`, `keyupdate`, and `resumption` cells, preserve the advisory outcome classes, avoid recasting the cluster as an Incursa-side transport defect without new evidence, and remain outside ordinary push, pull-request, build, test, package, and support-readiness gates.
notes: This formalizes the peer-side blocked lane only. It does not claim a local transport bug or a fix for msquic.
The quic-go client download-liveness slice remains the only local candidate in the major-peer evidence set.

requirements.title: Classify the connectionmigration source-address blocker as a distinct hosted proof lane
requirements.statement: The repository MUST preserve the hosted `connectionmigration-server-proof` lane as a bounded completed source-address proof only when a fresh hosted run shows `connectionmigration` succeeded with the first server flight sourced from the original server address instead of the preferred migration address, later preferred-address path use, server PATH_CHALLENGE and client PATH_RESPONSE evidence for migrated-path validation, active-migration Destination Connection ID change, and a completed transfer; preserve the `preferred_lft 0` setup for the preferred migration address so the address remains reachable without becoming the kernel-preferred source for the original-path first flight; and remain outside ordinary push, pull-request, build, test, package, and support-readiness gates.
notes: Hosted run `26174181713` on 2026-05-20 closed the source-address blocker for the bounded `connectionmigration` proof lane at commit `9ee3266e`.
The preferred migration address stays configured with `preferred_lft 0` so the lane remains reachable for migration without hijacking the original-path first flight.
This does not claim `rebind-port`, `rebind-addr`, HTTP/3, or broad support-readiness.

requirements.title: Track simulator-backed correctness scenarios separately from support promotion
requirements.statement: The repository MUST define a simulator-backed scenario model that records each planned network-condition scenario with a stable scenario identifier, explicit classification as correctness, advisory-interop, or performance-only, the upstream simulator profile and source reference, exact parameters, the local role and peer shape, the requirement IDs being exercised or the accounting-only requirement anchor, the expected observable behavior, the required evidence bundle, the promotion status, separation from broad support claims until linked verification records passing evidence for the bounded requirement set, and separation between simulator settings as evidence inputs, requirement statements as normative claims, and verification artifacts as proof records.
notes: The upstream simulator supplies network conditions such as point-to-point delay, bandwidth, queue size, packet drop or corruption rates, droplists, blackhole windows, rebinding, and cross-traffic. The correctness claim still belongs to the linked requirement and verification evidence.
Advisory interop and performance-only scenarios can be tracked by the model, but they do not promote protocol correctness unless a separate mapped requirement set and passing evidence say so.
This slice tracks the scenario model plus the first narrow helper and test surface. It does not change runtime transport behavior, workflow dispatch, or broad support claims.

requirements.title: Provide a manual all-upstream implementation handshake matrix profile
requirements.statement: The repository MUST provide an explicit manually dispatched hosted-CI all-implementation handshake matrix profile that reads the upstream QUIC interop-runner implementation registry at dispatch time, runs Incursa.Quic as the local client against every upstream server-capable implementation slot, runs Incursa.Quic as the local server against every upstream client-capable implementation slot, uses the `handshake` testcase only, uploads a distinct artifact bundle for every attempted role and peer cell, and remains advisory, opt-in, outside ordinary push, pull-request, build, test, package, upstream-runner-registry, and support-readiness gates.
notes: The upstream registry source is `implementations_quic.json` from `quic-interop/quic-interop-runner`; role compatibility derives from each entry's `role` field.

Client-role all-upstream cells may receive a runner-generated response body whose source file is mounted only into the peer server container; the harness uses the known source-length completion boundary when that local source file is available and otherwise reads the response until peer FIN under the existing response timeout.
The local helper accepts `-PeerImplementationSlots all` for role-aware local planning, but the hosted profile keeps this first all-upstream surface handshake-only.
This profile is evidence collection and peer characterization, not a broad interop-readiness or protocol-correctness claim for every testcase.

requirements.title: Open ngtcp2 short-header response packets with reconstructed packet numbers
requirements.statement: When running as a managed client against an upstream server that has already sent 1-RTT packets with high packet numbers, the receive path MUST reconstruct truncated short-header packet numbers from the current Application Data receive packet-number expectation before building the AEAD nonce, authenticate and process a one-byte truncated 1-RTT response packet whose full packet number is recoverable from prior received packets, preserve the normal peer FIN response-read completion path, and keep this as a bounded packet-opening correction rather than a broad support-readiness claim for every upstream implementation or testcase.
notes: The representative packet is the ngtcp2 server response from local run `.artifacts/interop-runner/ngtcp2-app-rx-debug3/20260519-002720755-client-chrome`, where server packet number 399463276 was truncated to one byte on the wire.
The proof remains bounded to packet opening and response liveness for the representative ngtcp2 handshake cell.

requirements.title: Trace the xquic client-role non-handshake liveness residual
requirements.statement: The repository MUST keep the remaining xquic client-role all-upstream `transfer`, `keyupdate`, and `chacha20` residual trace-owned before any transport change is promoted by preserving the broad May 19 all-upstream sweep plus focused May 19 and May 22 xquic rerun evidence, distinguishing the residual from the already-closed generic ordered-read wake-up and ACK-threshold issues, classifying it as an xquic-specific ingress, packet-opening, or path-liveness investigation until narrowed by new proof, and avoiding converting mostly-green all-upstream evidence into broad support-readiness claims.
notes: The current preserved evidence includes `.artifacts/interop-runner/all-upstream-streamdata-keyupdate-local/client/20260519-121832639-client-chrome`, `.artifacts/interop-runner/debug-client-transfer-xquic-after-ack-threshold/20260519-140609871-client-chrome`, `.artifacts/interop-runner/debug-client-transfer-xquic-current-after-docker-cleanup/20260522-221632093-client-chrome`, and `.artifacts/interop-runner/debug-client-transfer-xquic-live-refresh/20260523-161053951-client-chrome`.

The May 23 captured-packet proof opens a client-to-xquic 1-RTT packet from the May 22 rerun and verifies that it carries an ACK for xquic response packet 17 plus a MAX_DATA frame; this narrows the next investigation toward peer delivery and xquic event-loop packet processing rather than missing client ACK emission.

The multi-packet May 23 proof opens client packet numbers 13 through 28 from the same rerun and verifies an alternating post-burst MAX_DATA/MAX_STREAM_DATA credit sequence with strictly increasing advertised limits, so missing local credit emission is no longer the leading hypothesis.

The local interop-runner helper now reports that preserved packet/key material confirms valid post-burst ACK traffic while the xquic server-log short-header packet-processing ceiling through packets 0..3 remains a non-promoting failure diagnostic so a failed run points maintainers at post-burst ACK consumption, peer delivery, and xquic event-loop packet processing without treating the cell as passed.

The fresh May 23 live rerun under `.artifacts/interop-runner/debug-client-transfer-xquic-live-refresh/20260523-161053951-client-chrome` reaches `xqc_process_read_streams|stream_read_notify|flag:66` after the request stream is fully received, and the response burst runs through packet 22 before `xqc_send_packet_pacer_allows|pacing blocked` at `stream_offset:16536` prevents the transfer from draining to FIN, so the remaining runtime suspicion is post-send drain, pacing wakeup, peer delivery, and stream-drain behavior rather than packet opening or local ACK emission.
This is a trace ownership requirement for the residual investigation; it does not claim xquic interop support or authorize broad transport changes without a later focused proof slice.

requirements.title: Support the QUIC interop-runner HTTP/3 endpoint cell
requirements.statement: The interop harness MUST support `TESTCASE=http3` as a bounded QUIC interop-runner endpoint cell by using the existing managed QUIC transport with ALPN `h3`, starting the server endpoint on UDP port 443, loading `/certs/cert.pem` and `/certs/priv.key`, serving HTTP/3 GET responses from `/www`, reading client request URLs from `REQUESTS`, writing downloaded response bodies to `/downloads`, returning exit code `0` only after all requested downloads complete, returning exit code `1` for supported-cell failures, returning exit code `127` for unsupported test cases, emitting HTTP/3 diagnostic qlog events when `QLOGDIR` is set, preserving TLS secret export through `SSLKEYLOGFILE` when supported, and keeping non-HTTP/3 test cases delegated to the existing harness dispatch paths.
notes: This requirement owns only the interop-runner adapter cell and endpoint packaging contract.
The HTTP/3 and QPACK protocol behavior remains owned by the HTTP/3 and QPACK modules rather than by the interop harness.
HTTP/3 qlog emission is implemented through an optional diagnostics sink so the HTTP/3 layer remains independent from qlog serialization.
The first CI surface is advisory/local-runner evidence for the `http3` cell and does not claim upstream-registry participation or broad peer support.

requirements.title: Provide an advisory external HTTP/3 peer harness
requirements.statement: The repository MUST provide an advisory external HTTP/3 interop harness that defines Docker Compose targets for Incursa.Quic client/server, curl, aioquic, quiche or h3i, and ngtcp2/nghttp3 where available; defines scenarios for small, empty, large, concurrent, 404, many-header, split-DATA, cancellation, GOAWAY, and in-flight close behavior; provides Windows and POSIX execution scripts; emits machine-readable per-target/per-scenario results; generates a Markdown pass/fail/skip report by peer implementation; retains stdout, stderr, command lines, decoded per-scenario summaries, qlog directories, TLS key logs, and caller-supplied packet captures; and keeps skipped or failed rows explicit rather than using the harness as broad HTTP/3 or QPACK support promotion.
notes: Target identifiers are `incursa-client__incursa-server`, `curl__incursa-server`, `aioquic-client__incursa-server`, `quiche-client__incursa-server`, `ngtcp2-client__incursa-server`, `incursa-client__aioquic-server`, `incursa-client__quiche-server`, and `incursa-client__ngtcp2-server`.

Scenario identifiers are `get-small`, `get-empty`, `get-large`, `multiple-concurrent-get`, `not-found`, `many-headers`, `split-data`, `request-cancellation`, `goaway`, and `connection-close-in-flight`.
The artifact layout keeps scenario stdout/stderr and decoded summaries separate from service-wide qlogs, TLS key logs, and copied packet captures.

The first harness slice executes the Incursa and curl client paths against the Incursa server for static GET/404 scenarios and records other target/scenario cells as skipped until their exact peer command or endpoint behavior is wired.
This is an external characterization harness, not the upstream QUIC interop runner and not a support-readiness gate.

requirements.title: Provide an advisory h3spec HTTP/3 server conformance pipeline
requirements.statement: The repository MUST provide an advisory h3spec HTTP/3 server conformance pipeline that starts the local Incursa HTTP/3 server with temporary fixtures and TLS materials, invokes h3spec with a pinned or explicitly supplied tool command, captures stdout and stderr, parses h3spec output into machine-readable results, identifies each failing h3spec case, maps HTTP/3 failures to RFC 9114 sections and QPACK failures to RFC 9204 sections plus current gap owners, emits a Markdown failure triage report with follow-up TODO rows, and keeps the pipeline opt-in or non-gating until protocol-owned requirements and verification evidence promote the underlying behavior.
notes: The h3spec executable shape is `h3spec [options] <host> <port>`; this harness keeps the executable configurable so local and CI environments can provide a native binary or wrapper.
The first CI path runs plan-only by default on pull requests and installs h3spec only for explicitly dispatched live runs.
Failures discovered by h3spec should become protocol-owned RFC 9114 or RFC 9204 follow-up work before they are promoted as implementation support claims.

requirements.title: Keep ProtocolLab package targets lane-separated
requirements.statement: The repository MUST produce ProtocolLab package v2 implementation archives through repo-owned templates and helper scripts such that `quic-dotnet-dev` advertises only HTTP/3 protocol and HTTP application scenarios, `quic-dotnet-raw-dev` advertises only protocol `quic`, workload family `quic.transport`, and scenarios `quic.transport.multiplex.100x64kb` and `quic.transport.duplex-streams`, raw package generation resolves adapter and server implementation projects only under the quic-dotnet repository root while using the public ProtocolLab checkout only for neutral package tooling, schema validation, component-package tooling, and shared contract/model projects, and raw run submission rejects HTTP/3 suite, protocol, scenario, or capability selections before packaging, upload, or controller submission instead of falling back to managed HTTP/3 helpers.
notes: The raw package target is an implementation package producer only; public ProtocolLab scenario-pack and test-executor component packages remain separate package inputs.
This requirement does not broaden raw QUIC validation beyond the two named transport scenarios and does not change HTTP/3 or QPACK protocol support claims.

Package dry-runs prove archive shape and metadata. Rack-lab jobs remain separate performance evidence and must record package identity, SHA-256, job ID, run ID, and outcome in verification artifacts when used for claims.
